title: Additional S-Box Assumptions for Arbitrarily Distributed Secrets
summary: One security corollary needs a particular S-box assumption while another does not; it remains open whether further assumptions yield a result for arbitrarily distributed secrets.

formal_statement.body: In the noisy leakage model considered for masked implementations, two security corollaries differ only in that one requires a particular assumption on the S-box, whereas the other does not. It remains unresolved whether additional assumptions on the S-box can be exploited to obtain a corresponding security result when the secrets are arbitrarily distributed.

scope.domain: Security analysis of masked implementations in the noisy leakage model, with emphasis on S-box assumptions.
assumptions: One of the two security corollaries requires a particular assumption on the S-box.
parameters: S-box, the nonlinear component whose additional assumptions may be exploited
Secrets, whose distribution may be arbitrary
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether additional assumptions on the S-box can be exploited to obtain a corresponding security result when the secrets are arbitrarily distributed.

citations.label: Prou? & Rivain’s Formal Security Proof of Masking, Revisited: Tight Bounds in the Noisy Leakage Model

progress.summary: The source compares Corollaries 10 and 11 and notes that only one requires a particular S-box assumption. It explicitly leaves open whether further S-box assumptions can help for arbitrarily distributed secrets.
